The air quality measured by the official stations of
[GIOŚ](https://powietrze.gios.gov.pl), the Polish Chief Inspectorate of
Environmental Protection (Główny Inspektorat Ochrony Środowiska): the Polish
air quality index and the pollutants, station by station, hour by hour.

Not affiliated with GIOŚ. The data come from its open API
(`api.gios.gov.pl`), used as GIOŚ publishes it.

## What it does

- Reads the GIOŚ stations you choose (10 at most), with no account and no key.
- Creates **one device per station**: the Polish air quality index (0 to 5)
  and its level as a word, the pollutants the station measures (PM2.5, PM10,
  NO₂, O₃, SO₂, CO, benzene) and the age of the data.
- Adds a **GIOŚ air quality** dashboard widget, two scene triggers (**air
  quality degraded**, **back to normal**) and a scene action **Get the air
  quality**.
- Finds a station by its name or city, or the nearest ones to your house.

Read only: the integration only reads public data.

## Requirements

- Gladys Assistant 5.3.0 or later.
- Internet access from Gladys to `api.gios.gov.pl`.
- To search around your house: its location, in **Settings → Houses**.

## Configuration

### Choose the stations

1. Open the integration's **Configuration** tab.
2. Click **Find a station**: type a name or a city (`Kraków`, `Gdansk`:
   accents are optional), or leave it empty to list the stations nearest to
   your house, with their distance.
3. Copy the numbers you want into **Stations**, separated by commas: for
   example `530, 401`. Save.
4. In the **Discovery** tab, add the stations to Gladys.

The [map of the stations](https://powietrze.gios.gov.pl/pjp/current) shows
them all.

### Other settings

- **Refresh**: every 30 minutes (default) or every hour. GIOŚ publishes hourly
  averages, a little after each hour: reading more often would bring nothing.
- **Language**: language of the feature names (set when a device is added, so
  choose it first) and of the scene texts. French by default.

The **Check the stations** button reads every station now and tells what each
one answers.

## Devices

One device per station, named `GIOŚ <station>`.

| Feature                             | Values                                    |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Air quality index                   | 0 to 5 (Polish index, below)              |
| Air quality                         | the level as a word, in your language     |
| PM2.5, PM10, NO₂, O₃, SO₂, CO, C₆H₆ | µg/m³, hourly average                     |
| Measurement age                     | minutes since the hour of the latest data |

Only the pollutants the station measures are created. CO and benzene have no
dedicated type in Gladys in µg/m³: they appear as plain values, named by their
formula.

The **Polish air quality index** (Polski indeks jakości powietrza) has six
levels: 0 Very good (Bardzo dobry), 1 Good (Dobry), 2 Moderate (Umiarkowany),
3 Sufficient (Dostateczny), 4 Bad (Zły), 5 Very bad (Bardzo zły). It is
computed by GIOŚ from PM2.5, PM10, NO₂, O₃ and SO₂; the worst one sets it.

A value older than 3 hours is no longer published as current: Gladys keeps
the last one with its date, and the widget says the data are outdated.

## Widget

**GIOŚ air quality**:

- with a station chosen: up to four pollutant tiles, the index level colored
  (green, orange, red) and the age of the data;
- without: one row per station, its level colored.

## Scenes

### Trigger: GIOŚ: air quality degraded

Fires when the index of a station rises to **Moderate** or worse, or gets
worse again (Moderate then Bad fires twice). Filters: the station, and the
**new level**: tick the levels from your threshold up (for example Bad and
Very bad). Information for the actions: station name, level, its index, the
previous index, the pollutant that sets the level, a ready-made summary.

### Trigger: GIOŚ: air quality back to normal

Fires when the index comes back to **Good** or **Very good** after a
degradation. Filters: the station, and the worst level the degradation
reached (tick the same levels as above to pair both scenes). Information: the
new level, the worst level reached, a summary.

The first index read after the installation sets the starting level and fires
nothing; a restart does not fire the same change twice.

### Action: GIOŚ: get the air quality

The air quality of one station, or of the station with the worst index:
summary, level, index, pollutant, PM2.5, PM10, NO₂, O₃ and the age of the data,
for the next actions (a message, a condition).

## Scene examples

- **Close the windows**: trigger _air quality degraded_ with the levels Bad and
  Very bad → send `{{triggerEvent.data.summary}}` and switch the ventilation
  off.
- **Air again**: trigger _back to normal_ with the same levels → send "You can
  open the windows again".
- **Morning briefing**: at 7:30, action _get the air quality_ without station,
  then send its summary in the morning message.
- **Purifier**: when the PM2.5 feature of your station goes above 25 µg/m³,
  switch the air purifier on.

## Troubleshooting

- **"No station yet"** on the Configuration screen: type at least one station
  number in **Stations**.
- **"not a GIOŚ station"** in the check: the number is not in the GIOŚ list;
  use **Find a station**.
- **No PM2.5 on a station that measures it**: some stations only have a manual
  PM2.5 sensor, whose results GIOŚ publishes weeks later. Only the automatic,
  hourly sensors are read.
- **"The GIOŚ API does not answer"**: the values are kept and read again at
  the next refresh. The Logs tab tells the error once, and its end.
- **Air quality index without value**: GIOŚ gives no index for this hour
  ("Brak indeksu"), for example after a measurement outage.
- Details in the integration's **Logs** tab (`LOG_LEVEL=debug` for more).

## Limits

- Hourly data, published by GIOŚ a little after each hour: the last hour is
  often still missing, and the values lag by 1 to 2 hours.
- These are measurements, not forecasts.
- GIOŚ limits its API (1500 requests per minute on the current data, 2 per
  minute on the station list): the integration reads 10 stations at most, one
  request per pollutant, and the station list once a day.
- The index triggers follow GIOŚ's hourly index as published: an index that
  hesitates between two levels fires each change.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings GIOŚ asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Polish air quality stations | `section` | No | Reads the official measuring stations of GIOŚ, the Polish Chief Inspectorate of Environmental Protection, through its open API (no account). Not affiliated with GIOŚ. |
| Stations | `string` | No | The numbers of the GIOŚ stations to read, separated by commas (10 at most). The "Find a station" button below gives them, by name or around a house. |
| Refresh | `select` | No | GIOŚ publishes hourly averages, a little after each hour. |
| Language | `select` | No | Language of the feature names (set when a device is added) and of the scene texts. |

## How to install GIOŚ in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: GIOŚ appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-gios:1.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-gios](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-gios).

GIOŚ requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

GIOŚ is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [guim31](https://github.com/guim31), not by the Gladys core team.
